# Building Permit Processing Agent — Production Runbook

> **Scenario**: Building Permit Processing Agent
> **Platform**: Microsoft Copilot Studio — GitHub Copilot harness
> **Target readers**: Makers, delivery engineers, customer or partner operators

**Estimated effort**: Not yet measured; record actual effort on the Frontier Clock.

**Template:** an example to modify for your requirements; the customer or partner wires it into their environment. See the [Overview](1.Overview.md).

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build workload | 24 captured build checkpoints; 7 skills; 2 knowledge files; 5 acceptance checks; 5 locked cases. [Inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components), [checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks), and [cases](4.Sample-prompts.md#demo-prompts). | Template |
| Licensing and capacity | Confirm licensing for your tenant and Copilot Credits for building and testing the GitHub Copilot harness agent; do not assume the unpublished permit workshop is free to run. | Customer or partner |
| Environment and maker access | Record the approved permit environment, publisher prefix and maker access. Confirm the reviewed Sonnet46 model is available without changing the workshop's Draft boundary. | Customer or partner |
| DLP and data policy | Have the administrator review uploaded permit documents, proposed Dynamics 365 Customer Service, SharePoint and Microsoft Teams access, and channel restrictions; document rather than bypass blocked paths. | Customer or partner |
| Identity and audience | Review GroupMembership access, Integrated authentication and the Always authentication trigger in the supplied settings; name the maker, staff audience and production access approver. | Customer or partner |
| Connection ownership | Name owners for permit records, plan documents and field coordination. Record dedicated target-environment references and read-only identities; leave live connections out of the workshop. | Customer or partner |
| Test identities | Prepare technician, reviewer, inspector and denied-access identities for an approved test deployment. Makers use Draft Preview; sharing must not become a reason to publish the workshop. | Customer or partner |
| Easy-mode tooling | Use the Microsoft Copilot Studio plugin and PAC CLI 2.9.3 or newer for cli-copilot authoring. | Customer or partner |
| Manual build tooling | Use the Copilot Studio browser and reviewed uploads; no PAC CLI, YAML import or plugin architect. | Customer or partner |
| Municipal rule ownership | Have the permit owner approve real intake, review clocks, fee schedules and inspection-review responsibilities before replacing the fixed fictional records and rules. | Customer or partner |

## Phase 0 — Qualify and Adapt the Template

### Step 0-1. Qualify the outcome and baseline

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Permit service owner

Complete the [qualification checklist](1.Overview.md#qualification-checklist).

**Measure:** Permit backlog and review-clock status by permit type. Agree the starting queue and clock status before assessing intake, routing or applicant-update changes.

Fill your baseline record:

| Permit | Type | Reviewer | Cycle | Age | Target | Days over | Snapshot state |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

Agree permit replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures.

### Step 0-2. Adapt scope and name owners

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Permit service owner

Adapt [scope](1.Overview.md#in-scope--out-of-scope) and the [data contract](2.Architecture.md#data-contract); assign approval roles.

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Permit service owner | Approve intake, review-clock and escalation rules and production success measures; distinguish recommendations from authorized municipal decisions. |
| Plan reviewers and inspection lead | Review checklist scope, routing and coverage recommendations; retain permit, compliance and inspection decisions instead of delegating them to the synthetic agent. |
| Copilot Studio maker | Preserve the fixed snapshot, reviewed instructions, two knowledge files and all seven skills; capture the actual inspector-skill validation outcome and keep the build Draft. |
| Power Platform administrator | Confirm tenant licensing, capacity, environment access, authenticated audience and data policies before production permit integrations are enabled. |
| Municipal connection owners | Approve dedicated Dynamics 365 Customer Service, SharePoint and Microsoft Teams references, their identities and read-only access; own connection failures and replacements. |
| Acceptance reviewer | Review locked permit cases and chosen-lane evidence; confirm any build comparison uses matching inputs/model and the target remains Draft. |
| Operations owner | Own production session and credit monitoring, support and configuration recovery; escalate permit, fee and inspection decisions to the responsible human reviewers. |

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Permit replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures have named agreement.
- [ ] The permit owner records backlog, permit-type clocks and correction status before choosing customer success measures.

## Phase 2 — Build and Prove the Agent

### Step 2-1. Choose the build lane

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

| Lane | Suits | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy mode with GitHub Copilot (default) | Assisted authoring | Synthetic Draft proof |
| Manual build in Copilot Studio | Browser-only makers | Same Draft proof |

[Compare lanes](1.Overview.md#delivery-lanes); local Brainstem remains optional.

### Step 2-2. Build the selected implementation

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

**Easy mode:** use the [authoring skill](../../skills/aibast-easy-mode-copilot/SKILL.md) and [reviewed messages](../../solutions/building-permit-processing/EASY-MODE-COPILOT-CHAT.md). **Manual:** use the [single inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components) and [tutorial](https://microsoft.github.io/aibast-agents-library/solutions/building-permit-processing/manual-tutorial.html) with the checklist below. **Portable learning:** follow [deployment.json](../../solutions/building-permit-processing/deployment.json); it does not replace native Draft validation.

**Manual build checklist** — [captured sequence](../../solutions/building-permit-processing/screenshots/manual/browserfilm.json). Record real results, not manufactured historical failures.

1. 1 · Create a blank Copilot Studio agent
2. 2 · Name the manual agent

5. 5 · Open the knowledge-source picker
6. 6 · Upload the synthetic permit records
7. 7 · Wait for Dataverse ingestion
8. 8 · Upload the rules and schedules
9. 9 · Verify both knowledge sources
10. 10 · Open the SKILL.md uploader
11. 11 · Add backlog and complaint-risk logic
12. 12 · Add intake triage and routing
13. 13 · Add proactive applicant updates
14. 14 · Add permit status and zoning detail
15. 15 · Add the review checklist
16. 16 · Historical SKILL.md validation failure
17. 17 · Historical inspector skill retry
18. 18 · Add deterministic fee estimates
19. 19 · Review the available model choices
20. 20 · Match the Easy-mode model
21. 21 · Audit every skill description
22. 22 · Open Preview
23. 23 · Run the canonical backlog prompt
24. 24 · Verify the same permit and decision

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Apply the [workshop integrity and recovery rules](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) before replay.

### Step 2-4. Replay the synthetic proof

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

**Synthetic demo acceptance:** record every locked case: BPP-01, BPP-02, BPP-03, BPP-04, BPP-05. Use the [acceptance matrix](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [template acceptance checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks).

Fixed footer ([policy](../../solutions/building-permit-processing/manual/GLOBAL-INSTRUCTIONS.md)):

> Synthetic pilot data as of 2026-08-07; no live municipal system was accessed or changed.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] This lane's permit Preview evidence identifies the current agent, model, inventory and Draft state.
- [ ] If chosen, the recipe smoke test calls `BuildingPermitProcessingAgent` and returns its required markers.
- [ ] Record completion or non-use of the optional permit track without claiming an unperformed validation.
- [ ] The manual permit inventory has two knowledge files, seven skills, reviewed instructions and the confirmed model.
- [ ] The inspector-skill checkpoint has current acceptance evidence, not a staged recreation of the historical failure.
- [ ] Unchanged permit prompts pass in separate fresh Preview chats on the owned Draft.
- [ ] Every permit case is judged on its complete final response, not a visual checkpoint alone.
- [ ] Chosen-lane proof is complete; any Easy/Manual comparison has matching inputs and model.

## Phase 3 — Wire In Your Systems

### Step 3-1. Integrate Dynamics 365 Customer Service

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Municipal connection owners

1. **Bind Dynamics 365 Customer Service — read:** Bind approved read-only permit actions.

2. **Identity for Dynamics 365 Customer Service:** Decide end-user versus approved maker/service credentials; [Configure authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication) for the [authorized audience](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions).

3. **Scope Dynamics 365 Customer Service:** Require sign-in for restricted permit information. Request only scopes needed for approved records and actions. Restrict the staff audience and test authorized and denied access. Enforce restrictions at the connection.

4. **Exit test for Dynamics 365 Customer Service:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 8](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): State that the ID is absent and list known synthetic IDs; never substitute another permit. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): State what is missing, list known matches or clarify; never default to another permit.

Map records to Dynamics 365 Customer Service, plans to SharePoint and coordination to Microsoft Teams; start approved connections read-only.

### Step 3-2. Integrate SharePoint

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Municipal connection owners

1. **Bind SharePoint — read:** Add approved plan and policy knowledge with a content owner.

2. **Identity for SharePoint:** Decide end-user versus approved maker/service credentials; [Configure authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication) for the [authorized audience](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions).

3. **Scope SharePoint:** Require sign-in for restricted permit information. Request only scopes needed for approved records and actions. Restrict the staff audience and test authorized and denied access. Enforce restrictions at the connection.

4. **Exit test for SharePoint:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 2](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Do not accept the submission or assign anyone; recommend intake corrections and routing for human review. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim that a lookup, permit change or message succeeded.

### Step 3-3. Integrate Microsoft Teams

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Municipal connection owners

1. **Bind Microsoft Teams — read-write:** Start read-only; gate sending or assignment workflows behind approval (preview).

2. **Identity for Microsoft Teams:** Decide end-user versus approved maker/service credentials; [Configure authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication) for the [authorized audience](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions).

3. **Scope Microsoft Teams:** Require sign-in for restricted permit information. Request only scopes needed for approved records and actions. Restrict the staff audience and test authorized and denied access. Enforce restrictions at the connection.

4. **Exit test for Microsoft Teams:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 3](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Produce drafts only; never report messages as sent, delivered or acknowledged. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Return a recommendation or draft; any future write requires separate governance and human approval.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Approved record, document and coordination connections start read-only; writes retain separate governance and human approval.
- [ ] Approved replacement connections preserve the reviewed permit input/output contract; no system change is claimed without successful tool evidence.

## Phase 4 — Evaluate on Your Data

### Step 4-1. Adapt the evaluation corpus

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Preserve [locked behaviors](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [boundary tests](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases) when substituting approved customer fixtures.

### Step 4-2. Set thresholds and evaluate your data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Have the business owner approve thresholds. Run [adapted evaluations (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-agent-evaluation-intro) before publication under approved test user profiles. Keep exact assertions separate from General quality scores.

Run pre-publication evaluations of adapted permit cases with approved test user profiles; verify exact assertions separately from General quality scores.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The business owner sets customer-data acceptance measures; synthetic records are not customer KPIs or measured production results.
- [ ] Adapted evaluations record the tested version and user profile; General quality scoring does not replace exact assertions.

## Phase 5 — Pilot and Rollout

### Step 5-1. Review the template release prerequisites

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

These synthetic regression gates do not set production thresholds. The reference workshop stays Draft; production approval belongs to the customer pilot.

| Template gate | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Locked permit corpus | All five cases, BPP-01 through BPP-05, satisfy every required and forbidden marker. |
| Full workflow inventory | Two knowledge files, seven skills, reviewed instructions and model; no workshop tools. |
| Inspector-skill validation | The inspector skill is accepted and visible; retry only after a recorded genuine error. |
| Municipal authority boundary | Any permit change, sent message, inspection action, fee transaction or compliance certification is no-go. |
| Visual evidence | Require current-agent target-state anchors; blank, historical published-pilot and reshoot-required frames cannot pass. |
| Draft release | The manual release agent remains unpublished; the historical published pilot is excluded. |

### Step 5-2. Publish and share deliberately

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Permit service owner

With business approval, [publish and share](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent) the adapted build with a restricted test audience. Keep the reference workshop Draft.

Obtain explicit confirmation for the production publish operation.

### Step 5-3. Run the governed pilot

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Permit service owner

**Pilot entry gate:** Test allowed and denied identities on the published, shared agent; resolve access failures before admitting pilot users. Compare pilot results with the baseline and thresholds; broaden rollout only after go/no-go.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Production publication has explicit confirmation independent of the historical pilot.
- [ ] After restricted publication and sharing, approved permit staff can access the channel and unshared test identities are denied before pilot entry.

## Phase 6 — Operate

### Step 6-1. Retain the operational playbook

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Operations owner

The template provides the [state-and-recovery playbook](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) and regression cases.

### Step 6-2. Own changes and ongoing verification

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Operations owner

Review content freshness and permissions; re-evaluate source, model, skill or connector changes. [Monitor the deployed agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-overview).

Review failed permit sessions, wrong-record answers, connection errors and credit consumption in Monitor.

### Step 6-3. Release: ALM

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

Back up the permit workspace, pull before editing and pushing, then create the package with `pac copilot pack`.

### Step 6-4. Release: recovery

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Verify backup and restore eligibility for the permit environment; rehearse recovery to a supported test target.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The permit environment's recovery rehearsal uses an eligible source type and supported restore target.
- [ ] The operator reviews failed sessions, source usage, authentication errors and credit consumption after rollout.
